title: Qt: Update Packet Details on color rule changes
description:
The Packet Details pane did not refresh when display coloring rules were
modified, leaving stale colors until another UI event forced a redraw. Connect
the Packet Details to the colorsChange signal/slot and trigger an update
so the pane immediately reflects current coloring rules.

This improves consistency across the UI and removes the need for manual
interaction to see updated colors.

Fixes #20774.

I don't understand this change.

1. You mix colorsChanged signal with updating styleSheet. The styleSheet updates should be done as a part of QEvent::ApplicationPaletteChange(), then it will also work when system color scheme changes (not only from Wireshark preferences). This does not belong in the preferences colorsChanged signal.
2. You add set_style_sheet_ which is never used for anything.
3. You check prefs.gui_active_style, prefs.gui_inactive_style and prefs.gui_packet_list_hover_style for StatusBar. When is this used?
4. You do the same as 3. in DataSourceTab. When is this used?
5. You use gradient_style_format in DataSourceTab. When is this used?

I think you are trying to fix the styleSheet update using the wrong approach?

Thanks for the clarification.

I originally followed the approach used in PacketList::colorsChanged, but if styleSheet updates are intended to be handled in QEvent::ApplicationPaletteChange, then the correct place should indeed WiresharkMainWindow::updateStyleSheet I guess.

I will refactor the changes accordingly:

1. Add dedicated updateStyleSheet() methods to both DataSourceTab and MainStatusBar.
2. Remove the colorsChanged-based updates and instead trigger the style refresh from WiresharkMainWindow::updateStyleSheet.
3. Drop the unused set_style_sheet_ and the incorrect checks on prefs.gui_*_style.

This should align the implementation with the expected palette-change flow.
I’m still getting familiar with the Wireshark codebase, so your guidance is appreciated.
Applied above changes as only 1 main commit.

Unneeded whitespace change
I want to understand if we could update the stylesheet without this hack, it doesn't look right.

I tried `style()->polish(this)` in MainStatusBar::updateStyleSheet() for the status bar. I was thinking the other widgets would behave the same, but they probably don't. Maybe this also depends on where you change the settings, if it's in Wireshark preferences or System Settings.

When the base palette is changed, ApplicationPaletteChanged gets sent to all top level windows, and those send PaletteChanged to child widgets, and everything using the default QPalette from the QStyle is updated - if style sheets are not used.

If CSS-style style sheets are used, then Qt does not update the colors, assuming that you'd want to continue using the style sheet colors, which is usually true but less so when the style sheet colors are also derived from the application default palette. (Adding a stylesheet changes the QStyle for a widget to QStyleSheetStyle.)

Style sheets also by default prevent the PaletteChanged signals from propagating to children.

Style sheets also don't by default propagating changes in their fonts and palette set via style sheet to their children, but setting the application attribute Qt::AA_UseStyleSheetPropagationInWidgetStyles to true can change that. We might want to do that, though it could possibly change the appearance of some child widgets.

Removing the application style sheet from 09c98896fe8ba549c7f396ced46e35b7d53255ac and implementing the "make all QMessageBoxes allow text selection via mouse" via a QProxyStyle would make palette changes from switching the style or dark mode propagate more.

This is less of an issue on Windows, specifically, because we switch from the WindowsVista QStyle to the Fusion QStyle when going to dark mode, which causes all the widgets to paint themselves, as mentioned above.

This should be done on other platforms. In particular Linux. It happens to be less necessary on Windows, but that's is only because in `main_application.cpp` Windows changes color schemes between WindowVista and Fusion when the color scheme becomes light or dark, which has the side effect of causing everything to repaint.

Also, probably call this in the ProtoTree constructor instead of having the same text in two places.
